review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no @[simp] attributes. I grepped the repo for uses of the booleanCoefficient_*, formProduct_nil/cons and normalMonomial_eval lemmas, and read several call sites (ForecastInactiveProduct, RealKernelJetInverse, IntegerAffineResidues, NormalizedIntegerDual). I did not run Lean. I did not check whether adding these attributes would cause simp conflicts or break downstream proofs, and the suggestions rest on reading the statements. I judged booleanCoefficient_map and booleanCoefficient_monomial unsuitable as default simp lemmas: the first is used in both directions, and the second is an ite-producing characterisation. findings.excerpt: theorem booleanCoefficient_const_mul {α R : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [CommRing R]
findings.problem: The linearity lemmas for booleanCoefficient (sum, const_mul, add, div) are not simp lemmas. Their left-hand sides are the canonical form to push through: `booleanCoefficient (fun t => ∑ i ∈ b, f i t) s`, `fun t => c * f t`, `fun t => f t + g t` and `fun t => f t / a`. Downstream files always list them by hand as a fixed bundle, e.g. `simp only [map_sum, map_mul, MvPolynomial.eval_C, booleanCoefficient_sum, booleanCoefficient_const_mul]` and `simp_rw [he, booleanCoefficient_add, booleanCoefficient_sum, booleanCoefficient_const_mul]`. The bundle is copied between the real and integer jet-matrix files. So the simp set for this operator is spread over call sites instead of being declared once.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `booleanCoefficient_add`, `booleanCoefficient_sum`, `booleanCoefficient_const_mul` and `booleanCoefficient_div` as `@[simp]`, or put them in a dedicated simp set such as `booleanCoefficient_linear` if global simp is thought too aggressive. Each lemma strictly pushes `booleanCoefficient` inward and terminates. Then `simp [map_sum, MvPolynomial.eval_C]` can replace the repeated `simp only` lists. `booleanCoefficient_map` should stay un-simp, since both orientations are used. A matching `booleanCoefficient_sub`/`_neg`/`_zero` is worth adding for a complete interface. The only proved subtraction statement is the bound `booleanCoefficient_sub_bound`.
findings.benefit: Call sites stop restating the same four-lemma bundle. A normal form is fixed for jets of sums and scalar multiples, so new proofs get this behaviour from plain `simp`.

findings.excerpt: booleanCoefficient (fun _ => c) s = if s = ∅ then c else 0
findings.problem: The only simp-oriented statement about constants leaves an `if s = ∅` that simp cannot discharge when the index type is empty. There is no companion lemma for `IsEmpty α`, where every `s` is `∅`. At least nine call sites in other files repeat the same ad hoc line `simp only [booleanCoefficient_const, (Subsingleton.elim t ∅ : t = ∅), ↓reduceIte]` to prove `booleanCoefficient (fun _ : Finset Empty => z) t = z`. Other users, such as the `AllocatedInactive*Support` files, rewrite with `booleanCoefficient_const` and then handle the conditional by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma `booleanCoefficient_const_of_isEmpty [IsEmpty α] (c : R) (s : Finset α) : booleanCoefficient (fun _ => c) s = c`. It follows from `booleanCoefficient_const` plus `Subsingleton.elim s ∅`. Mark it `@[simp]`, because its side condition is a typeclass argument and not a hypothesis. Then restate `booleanCoefficient_const` as `@[simp]` only if the `ite` form is wanted as a default; otherwise keep it as a plain rewrite lemma.
findings.benefit: The repeated `Subsingleton.elim` plus `↓reduceIte` incantation and the local `hc` helper lemmas disappear. The empty-index degenerate case reduces by plain `simp`.

findings.excerpt: theorem formProduct_nil {α β R : Type*} [CommRing R] :
findings.problem: `formProduct` is a plain noncomputable def over a list. Its two defining equations are stated as `rfl` lemmas but are not simp lemmas, and `formProduct` is not `@[simp]`-unfoldable. Every consumer therefore has to name them explicitly, both in this file and elsewhere: `simpa only [formProduct_cons, List.length_cons, Nat.add_comm]`, `rw [formProduct_cons, normalWord_product, map_mul, ...]` and `simp only [formProduct_cons, map_mul, ...]`. Elsewhere there is `simp [formProduct_nil]` and `... formProduct_cons]`. Without simp, `simp` cannot see through `formProduct (f :: l)` and stalls on the unexpanded product.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `formProduct_nil` and `formProduct_cons` `@[simp]`. They are structural recursion equations in the constructor direction, and `formProduct_cons` strictly decreases list length, so there is no cycle. Consider also marking `normalWord_product` simp, since it rewrites to the canonical `normalMonomial` form.
findings.benefit: Proofs about list products, such as the vanishing-product lemmas, can use plain `simp`. The explicit equation lemmas drop out of the rewrite lists at lines 177, 209, 361 and 383 and in NormalizedIntegerDual.

findings.declaration: site / formPolynomial (no evaluation lemmas); used in normalMonomial_eval and normalMonomial_mul_coordinate
findings.excerpt: simp only [formProduct_cons, map_mul, formPolynomial, eval_X, site, zero_mul]
findings.problem: `site` and `formPolynomial` are defined by pattern matching but come with no named simp or equation lemmas for the evaluations that actually occur: `eval (site s) (X none) = 1`, `eval (site s) (X (some (.inl i))) = if i ∈ s then 1 else 0`, `eval (site s) (X (some (.inr j))) = 0` and the value of a difference form. The proofs unfold the whole definitions instead, with `simp only [..., site, ...]` at line 300 and `simp [formPolynomial, site, hst, hst hi]` at line 363. That exposes the case-split bodies and leaves the normal form to whatever simp does with the unfolded match.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` lemmas `site_none : site s none = 1`, `site_inl : site s (some (.inl i)) = if i ∈ s then 1 else 0` and `site_inr : site s (some (.inr j)) = 0`. Add `@[simp] formPolynomial_coordinate`/`formPolynomial_difference` for the two constructors. Then write `eval (site s) (formPolynomial (.difference i)) = (if i ∈ s then 1 else 0) - 1` as a simp lemma. Call sites would use `simp` without unfolding `site` or `formPolynomial`.
findings.benefit: The simp normal form for evaluation at a Boolean site is stated once. Proofs no longer depend on the internal match structure of `site` and `formPolynomial`.
